countermeasures.title: Harden HART Maintenance-level write authentication to HMI-equivalent strength
countermeasures.description: Implement the HART (IF-2) write-authentication mechanism required by REQC003: a credential mechanism at least as strong as the local HMI's role-credential model (AS-2), with rate-limiting/lockout equivalent to AS-12. Closes the still-open choice of exact HART authentication mechanism to a concrete, testable minimum bar rather than leaving it undefined.

countermeasures.title: Local confirmation / write-protect gate for remote Modbus RTU configuration writes
countermeasures.description: Implements a product-level gate on Modbus RTU (IF-3) writes to operational configuration registers: a local HMI confirmation step, or a physical/soft write-protect toggle, so a device on the shared bus cannot silently apply configuration changes without local acknowledgement. Deployment-level bus segmentation (AS-6, REQC001) remains a complementary compensating control.
negativeEffects: Adds a local-confirmation step to remote/scripted commissioning workflows that previously applied Modbus configuration writes without any on-device interaction.

countermeasures.title: Firmware update-time signature and version/anti-rollback verification
countermeasures.description: The existing, already-implemented update-time mitigation (AS-3): every incoming firmware image is checked for a valid cryptographic signature and a version that is not older than the currently installed one before it is applied, preventing straightforward malicious or rollback updates via IF-4/IF-5.

countermeasures.title: Local HMI PIN attempt lockout with increasing retry delay
countermeasures.description: The existing, already-implemented HMI protection (AS-12): a limited number of consecutive failed PIN attempts, increasing retry delay after repeated failures, and temporary lockout after excessive failures, satisfying REQC002.

countermeasures.title: Mandatory fuzz / malformed-input testing gate for protocol parsers
countermeasures.description: REQC005's release-blocking test requirement: HART, Modbus RTU, and Ethernet service-interface parsers are exercised with fuzz/malformed-input testing before each release, with crashes, hangs, or undefined behavior treated as release-blocking defects (tracked in 09-defects if found).
negativeEffects: Availability risk from a parser crash/hang remains open until this test gate is executed and passed; the watchdog (CM-8) already bounds the safety-impact dimension in the meantime.

countermeasures.title: TLS 1.2+ implementation with tested certificate/hostname validation
countermeasures.description: REQC004's concrete minimum bar for the Ethernet service interface (IF-4): TLS 1.2 or higher, device-unique certificate/key provisioned at manufacturing, non-deprecated cipher suites only, and certificate/hostname validation logic covered by dedicated test cases before release.

countermeasures.title: Force default-credential change on first commissioning boot
countermeasures.description: A product-level fix for T-8: require the Ethernet service interface's default credentials to be changed before the device leaves initial commissioning mode, rather than relying on procedural user-guide guidance (REQC001) alone. Not selected for the current product version; retained as a documented alternative should the accepted residual risk on T-8 later need to be revisited.
negativeEffects: Adds a mandatory commissioning-flow step (forced credential change) that increases first-boot complexity and support-desk burden for lost/forgotten credentials.
Not selected for v1; T-8 remains accepted on the existing procedural control instead.

countermeasures.title: Independent watchdog forces a fail-safe reset on firmware hang/crash/deadlock
countermeasures.description: The existing, already-decided design assumption (AS-18): an independent hardware watchdog detects a firmware hang, crash, task deadlock, or other loss of application control, resets the device, and forces the analog output to the defined fail-safe fault current during the reset/restart sequence rather than holding a stale value. This is what allows T-19's safety-impact dimension to be rated 1 instead of the worst case.

countermeasures.title: Document plant perimeter-security responsibility in the user guide
countermeasures.description: REQC001's requirement: the user guide must state the plant owner's/integrator's responsibility to physically secure the perimeter (loop wiring, RS-485 bus membership, tank/process area access) for the threats where the RL-100 itself cannot enforce protection (T-1, T-2, T-7, T-17). The user guide has not yet been drafted.

countermeasures.title: MCU JTAG/SWD production lockdown (readout protection) with controlled manufacturer recovery procedure
countermeasures.description: REQC006's requirement, grounded in AS-17: JTAG/SWD disabled or access-protected (RDP) in production firmware, with any factory-debug/recovery state requiring Manufacturer-support-level authorization (AS-1) and re-lock before the unit leaves manufacturer control. Narrows the debug-port bypass path for T-13 and the key-extraction path for T-11, and also narrows T-22's debug-access bypass route against the bootloader's write-protection (AS-19); T-12's external-flash chip-off vector is a separate physical attack path not addressed by this control.

countermeasures.title: Use validated cryptographic libraries for all cryptographic operations
countermeasures.description: REQC012's requirement: firmware-signature verification, TLS on IF-4, and all other cryptographic operations use a validated, actively-maintained cryptographic library (e.g. mbedTLS, wolfSSL, or an equivalent vetted implementation), including constant-time implementations for secret-dependent comparisons, instead of a custom/in-house implementation. Reduces the likelihood that implementation-level weaknesses (timing side-channels, faulty verification logic, weak random-number generation) undermine T-13's signature check or T-21's TLS session.

countermeasures.title: Resource-limiting and load/resource-exhaustion testing gate for protocol services
countermeasures.description: REQC013's requirement: HART, Modbus RTU, and Ethernet service-interface handling enforce resource limits (max concurrent connections, request-rate limiting, bounded per-connection buffer/state), exercised with a dedicated load/resource-exhaustion test gate before release, with resource exhaustion, hangs, or crashes under sustained load treated as release-blocking defects.
negativeEffects: Availability risk from resource exhaustion remains open until this control and its test gate are implemented and passed; the watchdog (CM-8) already bounds the safety-impact dimension in the meantime.

countermeasures.title: Replay protection (nonce/timestamp) on authenticated protocol writes
countermeasures.description: REQC014's requirement: authenticated write-capable protocol interfaces (HART IF-2 per REQC003, and any future networked configuration interface) bind each authenticated write to a nonce or timestamp so a captured legitimate write cannot be replayed later to reproduce its effect.

countermeasures.title: Documented key-management policy for firmware code-signing and bootloader provisioning
countermeasures.description: REQC007's requirement: firmware code-signing keys are generated, stored, and used under a documented key-management policy (e.g. HSM-backed, access restricted to named roles, dual control for key use, logged signing events) at manufacturing/provisioning, so the bootloader's root-of-trust material (AS-19) and AS-3's signature check are not undermined by weak protection of the signing key itself.
